High Court Of Madhya Pradesh
 At Gwalior

sentences.text: This miscellaneous appeal has been preferred by the appellants/claimants under Section 173(1) of the Motor Vehicles Act, 1988, being aggrieved by the Award dated 30.07.2005 passed by the Third Motor Accident Claims Tribunal, District Morena (M.P.) (hereinafter referred to as "the Claims Tribunal") in Claim Case No. 178/2004, on the grounds of inadequacy of compensation as well as exoneration of the Insurance Company from its liability.

entities.text: Third Motor Accident Claims Tribunal, District Morena
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text: The appellants seek enhancement of compensation and setting aside of the findings absolving the Insurance Company.

2. Brief facts of the case are that on 15.04.2004 at about 2:30 a.m., near Baba Devpuri Temple on A.B. Road, respondent No.2, by driving the tractor bearing registration No. UP-83-F-0078 along with a trolley owned by NEUTRAL CITATION NO. 2026:MPHC-GWL:4525 2 MA-1126-2005 respondent No.1 in a rash and negligent manner, overturned the same, as a result of which Gopal Singh, who was sitting in the trolley along with bags of seeds, died on the spot.
The said incident was reported at Police Station Sarai Chola, District Morena, against respondent No.2, whereupon a case under Section 304-A of IPC was registered as Crime No.33/2004.

entities.text: Police Station Sarai Chola, District Morena
entities.label: ORG

sentences.text:
After completion of investigation,
charge-sheet was filed before the competent Court.
3. On account of the death of Gopal Singh, the appellants submitted a claim petition before the Claims Tribunal seeking compensation.
Notices were issued to the respondents.

Respondents No.1 Mst. Sono Devi vs Babi Singh Parmar on 4 February, 2026 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/52763241/
1 and 3 filed their replies, whereas respondent No.2 remained ex parte.
Thereafter, issues were framed and the case was fixed for evidence.

4. After framing of issues and recording of evidence, the Claims Tribunal awarded compensation to the tune of Rs.1,17,000/- along with interest from the date of filing of the claim petition till realization.

5. Being aggrieved by the impugned Award, the appellants/claimants have preferred the present appeal contending that the learned Claims Tribunal failed to properly appreciate the evidence on record and awarded inadequate compensation.

It is contended that the deceased was a healthy person aged about 41 years and that the Claims Tribunal erred in assessing his income at Rs.1,250/-
per month, which is stated to be extremely low.
The appellants contended that the deceased was engaged in agricultural work and used to sell milk, earning Rs.72,000/- annually from agriculture and Rs.4,000/- per month from milk business.

It is further contended that despite NEUTRAL CITATION NO. 2026:MPHC-GWL:4525 3 MA-1126-2005 the appellants having led oral evidence on oath to establish the income of the deceased, and in the absence of any rebuttal evidence by the respondents, the Claims Tribunal erred in assessing the annual income at only Rs.15,000/-.
It is further contended that the deceased was sitting in the trolley along with seed bags meant for agricultural purposes, which was duly proved by the appellants.

Despite the same, the Claims Tribunal treated the deceased as a passenger in the tractor trolley and held that it was a violation of the insurance policy conditions, thereby wrongly exonerating the Insurance Company from liability.

According to the appellants, the tractor was being used for agricultural purposes and, therefore, the Insurance Company ought to have been held liable and just and proper amount of compensation be awarded.

6. On the other hand, learned counsel for respondent No.3/Insurance Company supported the impugned Award and submitted that the Claims Tribunal has rightly assessed the compensation and correctly exonerated the Insurance Company in view of the evidence available on record.
It is contended that the appeal is devoid of merit and deserves dismissal.
7. Heard learned counsel for the parties and perused the record of the Claims Tribunal.
8. On careful perusal of the record, it is found that the deceased was travelling in the tractor as a passenger and not as an agricultural labourer.
The tractor was being used at the time of accident for carrying baratis.
The FIR specifically mentions that the tractor was used for carrying passengers as baratis and not for agricultural purposes.
NEUTRAL CITATION NO. 2026:MPHC-GWL:4525 4 MA-1126-2005 9.

In regard to the contention that the tractor was being used for agricultural purposes and that the deceased was seated with the seeds, reliance has been placed on the decision of the Hon'ble Supreme Court in Oriental Insurance Company Ltd. Vs. Premlata Shukla and others , 2007 (3) TAC 11 (S.C.), wherein it has been held in paragraphs 13 and 14 as under:

2 "13.

sentences.text: However, the factum of an accident could also be proved from the First Information Report.

It is also to be noted that once a part of the contents of the document is admitted in evidence, the party bringing the same on record cannot be permitted to turn round and contend that the other contents contained in the rest part thereof had not been proved.
Both the parties have relied thereupon.
It was marked as an Exhibit as both the parties intended to rely upon them.

14. Once a part of it is relied upon by both the parties, the learned Tribunal cannot be said to have committed any illegality in relying upon the other part, irrespective of the contents of the document been proved or not.

If the contents have been proved,
the question of reliance thereupon only upon a part thereof and not upon the rest, on the technical ground that the same had not been proved in accordance with law,
would not arise."
10. In the present case, the FIR clearly mentions that the deceased was sitting in the tractor and that the tractor was being used for carrying passengers as baratis.
Thus, it is evident that the tractor was not being used for agricultural purposes at the time of the accident.

11. Since the deceased was travelling in the tractor either as a passenger or labourer, and no additional premium was paid for any passenger or labourer, the deceased cannot be treated as a third party for fastening liability on the Insurance Company.

12. In New India Assurance Co. Ltd. vs. Asha Rani , AIR 2003 SC 607, the Hon'ble Apex Court has held that since passengers are not permitted to be carried in a tractor, the Insurance Company cannot be saddled with NEUTRAL CITATION NO. 2026:MPHC-GWL:4525 5 MA-1126-2005 liability and compensation is recoverable only from the owner and driver of the vehicle.
13.

entities.text: New India Assurance Co. Ltd. vs. Asha Rani , AIR 2003 SC 607
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: In view of the above legal position, this Court is of the considered opinion that the Claims Tribunal has rightly exonerated the Insurance Company from liability.
The finding absolving respondent No.3 does not warrant any interference and the contention of the appellants seeking to fasten liability on the Insurance Company is rejected.

14. So far as contention of appellants/claimants regarding enhancement of compensation is considered, after hearing counsel for the parties and on perusal of record of the Claims Tribunal, it is found that the appellants/claimants have utterly failed to adduce any substantial evidence in regard to income of the deceased- Gopal.

Hence, this Court finds it appropriate to assess the income of the deceased as an unskilled person in view of the law laid down in the cases of Sukhdevi v.
Devendra Kumar , ILR 2014 MP 172; Kanwar Devi v. Bansal Roadways , 2008 ACJ 2182; and National Insurance Co. Ltd. v. Renu Devi , (2008) 3 ACC 134 in which it is held that when documentary proof of income is lacking, income is to be assessed as per the minimum wages applicable.

entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: As per Pranay Sethi (supra), future prospects @ 10% be assessed.

Further, as per the judgment NEUTRAL CITATION NO. 2026:MPHC-GWL:4525 6 MA-1126-2005 of the Apex Court in the case of Sarla Verma and ors. Vs Delhi Transport Corporation and Anr.
reported in (2009) 6 SCC 121, even if age of the claimant is to be taken into account, multiplier of 11 has rightly been applied.

sentences.text:
16. A ccordingly, the appellants/claimants are entitled to receive compensation under the following heads:-
 HEAD AMOUNT  Income Rs.2205 x 12= Rs.2  Future Prospects@10% Rs.29,106/-
 Dependency 3/4 Rs.21,830/-
 Multiplier 11 Rs.2,40,130/-
Other Heads:-
Loss of Consortium Rs.40,000 X 4 = Rs Loss of Estate and funeral expenses Rs.30,000/-
Thus, the just and proper amount of compensation payable in the present case comes to Rs.4,30,130/- as against the sum of Rs.1,17,000/- awarded by the learned Claims Tribunal.
Accordingly, the appellants/claimants are held entitled to an additional compensation of Rs.3,13,130/- over and above the amount already awarded by the Tribunal.20.

Consequently, the miscellaneous appeal is partly allowed, and the compensation amount is enhanced by Rs.3,13,130/-.
18.
The enhanced compensation shall carry interest at the same rate as awarded by the learned Claims Tribunal.
The enhanced amount shall be paid to the appellants within a period of three months from the date of receipt of the certified copy of this order.
The remaining conditions imposed by the learned Claims Tribunal shall remain intact.
NEUTRAL CITATION NO. 2026:MPHC-GWL:4525 7 MA-1126-2005 19.

In case the enhanced compensation exceeds the valuation of the appeal, the appellants shall deposit the differential Court fee (if not already paid) within a period of one month from today and furnish proof of such payment before the Registry.
Upon compliance, the Registry shall issue the certified copy of this order.
20. In view of the foregoing discussion, the miscellaneous appeal filed by the appellants/claimants stands disposed of accordingly.

(HIRDESH) JUDGE *AVI*
